title: When a Corporate Travel Programmes Booking Fee Stands as the Unit of the Service Charge
content:
Where a booking held in one of the Air Ticket Fare Brands carries a corporate programme reference, the unit the agency service charge is taken at comes from the Corporate Travel Programmes side rather than from the fare brand, and which of the programme's two booking fees applies is decided by the channel its fare lines were taken through.

## 1. The unit

| Where | The unit the charge is taken at is |
| --- | --- |
| a corporate programme reference stands on the booking and its fare lines were taken through the corporate portal | the programme's own online booking fee |
| a corporate programme reference stands on the booking and its fare lines were taken through any other channel | the programme's own offline booking fee |
| in every other case | no such substitution of the unit is made |

## 2. What is read, and from where

The reference read is the corporate programme reference standing on the air booking. The channel read is the channel recorded on the most recent base-fare line standing on that booking: the corporate portal, or anything else. The two booking fees are terms of the Corporate Travel Programmes programme the reference names, and are read from that programme's own record.

## 3. Points of judgement

**A booking with no corporate programme reference.** Neither of the first two rows can hold, because both open on such a reference standing on the booking.

**A booking whose reference stands but whose base fare was taken over the telephone service desk.** That is a channel other than the corporate portal, so the offline booking fee stands as the unit.

**A booking whose reference stands and whose base fare was taken through the corporate portal.** The online booking fee stands as the unit.
